text:
zoe: Dropping a follow-up thread from today's all-hands Q&A focused on a few edge-case questions we didn't get to: visas for international offsites, carbon offset policy for company travel, and hybrid meeting etiquette when the team is split across timezones. I'll collect replies and publish a one-pager.

michael: Thanks Zoe. First: I have a multi-week offsite in Berlin next quarter. Who handles visa letters, and how early should I start the process?

hr-director: Good Q. For work-related travel that requires a visa, start at least 8 weeks before departure. Submit the Travel Visa Request form and attach the offsite agenda + manager approval. People-ops will issue a visa support letter; legal will review any complex cases (e.g., paid speaking gigs, stipend recipients). If you're combining vacation with the offsite, we note it on the letter but still support processing.

people-ops-bot: Visa & international travel checklist uploaded: https://intranet.redwood/travel/visa_checklist (edited)

michael: Cool — any notes about per diem vs company card for long offsites (>7 days)?

hr-director: For long offsites we prefer to put lodging on a company card and use per diem for meals unless teams choose pooled expense tracking. If you need cash for incidentals, submit a Request for Advance at least 7 business days prior. Example expense flow:

```
1) Company card books hotel
2) Employee uses per diem $75/day for meals (international adjusted)
3) Submit receipts for any meals > per diem or non-standard expenses
```

zoe: New question: Is Redwood doing carbon offsets for flights? Someone suggested buying offsets for executive travel at the all-hands.

vp-people: We currently encourage lower-carbon options (train for <6hr trips, economy+ for red-eyes to avoid connections). We do not auto-purchase offsets for all flights yet. For Leadership-level travel, offsets can be requested via the Travel Offset Request and will be reviewed by Finance/Sustainability. We're evaluating a company-wide offset program; folks can opt into voluntary offsets via the expense flow and tag the expense "carbon-offset".

people-ops-bot: Sustainability pilot note: https://intranet.redwood/sustainability/travel_offsets (edited)

emma: For hybrid meeting etiquette: any guidance when 20% of the team is remote and the rest are in a room? We're seeing remote folks muted out of side convos.

it-security: Good callout. Short etiquette: 1) Always have a video and a dedicated remote-first mic. 2) If a subgroup breaks out in the room, assign a remote facilitator or move the breakout to a virtual room. 3) Recordings: we need consent if any external guests present.

zoe: Adding a small checklist for meeting hosts in the doc: - confirm AV, - add remote facilitator, - share agenda 24h prior, - avoid side conversations that shut out remote folks.

michael: What about bringing dependents/children for family circumstances? We have a parent who needs to travel with a child to an offsite.

hr-director: For dependent travel due to caregiving needs, managers can request a travel accommodation. We handle on a case-by-case basis and may approve partial reimbursement (lodging for family member split-pay) or childcare stipend for mandatory company time. Documentation & manager pre-approval required.

people-ops-bot: Accommodation request form: https://intranet.redwood/hr/accommodations (edited)

zoe: Any tip about booking multi-city itineraries for cost-saving? We sometimes have folks tack on another hub visit.

vp-people: Multi-city can be OK but needs manager approval and a clear business justification. Finance reserves the right to only reimburse the most economical single-destination route. If you choose a personal detour, that leg is self-pay. Always attach itinerary and cost comparison.

michael: Small ask: can we get a one-page flowchart showing who approves what (manager vs people-ops vs finance vs legal) for travel exceptions?

hr-director: Yes, we'll publish a one-pager. Volunteers to sanity-check the flow?

zoe: I can do a pass on wording.

it-security: One operational note: any offsite that requires access to internal tools from an external network must have an approved VPN exception and device check by IT at least 5 business days prior. No exceptions for sensitive infra access.

people-ops-bot: VPN exception & device checklist: https://intranet.redwood/it/vpn_device (edited)

vp-people: Thanks all. We'll consolidate this thread into the all-hands follow-up and pin it. Expect the visa checklist, travel offset pilot note, and hybrid meeting host checklist to be live by next Wednesday.

zoe: Thanks everyone 1. If you have edge cases DM me or open a ticket in #people-ops.
